Prehistoric India.Complete Notes:
PREHISTORIC INDIA

Prehistory refers to the period before the invention of writing. It is reconstructed through archaeological evidence such as tools, bones, and cave paintings.

Paleolithic Age (Old Stone Age):
• Time: 2.5 million BCE – 10,000 BCE
• Economy: Hunting and gathering
• Tools: Rough stone tools like hand axes and choppers
• Sites: Bhimbetka (MP), Hunsgi (Karnataka), Kurnool caves (AP)
• Lifestyle: Nomadic

Mesolithic Age (Middle Stone Age):
• Time: 10,000 BCE – 6000 BCE
• Tools: Microliths (small stone tools)
• Economy: Hunting, gathering, early domestication
• Sites: Bagor (Rajasthan), Adamgarh (MP)
• Transition phase towards settled life

Neolithic Age (New Stone Age):
• Time: 7000 BCE onwards
• Major change: Beginning of agriculture and animal domestication
• Tools: Polished stone tools
• Lifestyle: Settled life, village communities
• Sites: Mehrgarh (Pakistan), Burzahom (Kashmir), Chirand (Bihar)

Key Features:
• Transition from food gathering to food production
• Beginning of social organization and culture

Indus Valley Civilization.Complete Notes:
INDUS VALLEY CIVILIZATION

Time Period: 2500–1900 BCE

Major Sites:
• Harappa (Punjab)
• Mohenjo-daro (Sindh)
• Dholavira (Gujarat)
• Lothal (Gujarat)

Urban Planning:
• Grid pattern layout
• Advanced drainage system
• Citadel (upper town) and lower town
• Standardized bricks

Economy:
• Agriculture (wheat, barley)
• Trade with Mesopotamia
• Craft specialization (beads, pottery, seals)

Society:
• Urban, organized, possibly egalitarian

Religion:
• Mother Goddess worship
• Proto-Shiva (Pashupati seal)
• Animal and tree worship

Important Structures:
• Great Bath (Mohenjo-daro)
• Granaries
• Dockyard (Lothal)

Decline Theories:
• Climate change
• River shifts
• Ecological imbalance

Vedic Age.Complete Notes:
VEDIC AGE

Time Period: 1500–600 BCE

Divided into:

Early Vedic Period (1500–1000 BCE):
• Pastoral economy
• Tribal society (Jana)
• Political units led by Rajan
• Assemblies: Sabha and Samiti

Later Vedic Period (1000–600 BCE):
• Agriculture becomes dominant
• Use of iron tools
• Emergence of kingdoms (Janapadas)

Society:
• Varna system evolves (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras)

Religion:
• Early: Nature worship (Indra, Agni, Varuna)
• Later: Rituals and sacrifices increase

Literature:
• Vedas (Rig, Sama, Yajur, Atharva)
• Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads

Key Change:
• From tribal to territorial states
